sentences.text: Arrudatitan was relatively gracile compared to other titanosaurs.
The animal grew up to 15 meters long when fully grown.
Its femur measured 1.55 meters in length.
The type species A. maximus was originally described in 2011 as Aeolosaurus maximus before being moved to its own genus in 2021.
Based on the holotype, Arrudatitan reached a length of 15 meters when fully developed.
The femur of Arrudatitan measures 1.55 meters in length.

The holotype specimen MPMA 12-0001-97, containing partial vertebrae, ribs, chevrons, a scapula, arm bones, and leg bones, was discovered in 1997 by Ademir Frare and his 12-year-old nephew in Cândido Rodrigues.
Fernando Novas briefly noted the size of the holotype in 2009.
Arrudatitan is classified within the family Titanosauria.
It belongs to the family Aeolosauridae.
The species is placed in the tribe Aeolosaurini.
One cladistic analysis found Arrudatitan to be the sister group to Rinconsauria.
Another study suggested a close relationship to a group including Punatitan and other Aeolosaurus species.
Arrudatitan lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago, in what is now South America.
The time range for Arrudatitan is from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
